label: The three YAML workflows carry six check families absent from the chat path: pre_execution (threshold 70, hard block), planning_gate (threshold 70, critical, HALTED), post_execution (threshold 70), step_completion_rule, circuit_breaker CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN, and critical_steps verification.
The planning gate sits between planning and implementation (Between Step 7 and Step 8) with a 70/100 threshold and blocking review_integration; no chat-path check runs at that position in the work.

Three planning-gate checks have zero enforcement outside the YAMLs: spec_no_clarification (5 pts), checklist_verified (15 pts), review_approval (10 pts). A tree-wide search of .skilled/ excluding the three YAMLs returns no hits.

spec_no_clarification checks for a marker the current template set never writes: templates/core/ contains no NEEDS CLARIFICATION text, the validator registry has no rule for it, and the only consumer is a completeness score at calculate-completeness.sh:19.
Already duplicated on the chat path and must not be rebuilt: confidence thresholds 80/40, the strict validate.sh command string, the [SOURCE:] or UNKNOWN citation rule, and the retry ceiling of 3.

Completion-time checks are duplicated and the chat path's version is stronger: it requires the same tasks, acceptance-criteria and summary reconciliation plus a re-read of the request and its amendments, and is backed by AC_CLOSURE at error severity.

validate.sh already enforces the YAML file-shape family through FILE_EXISTS, LEVEL_MATCH, LEVEL_DECLARED, PLACEHOLDER_FILLED, SCAFFOLD_NEVER_TOUCHED, SPEC_DOC_SUFFICIENCY, TEMPLATE_SOURCE and AC_CLOSURE, so six of the YAML points add nothing a chat session does not already run.
The gap is sequencing plus judgment, not content: the chat path has every validator-decidable check and lacks every check positioned before implementation and every verdict that needs a reader.

A plan only its author can follow passes the chat path today: the authoring card section 6 acceptance is heading presence verified by a heading grep, section 7 anchors only task lines, and the card's own worked example is unanchored prose that satisfies both gates.

Smallest fix for the author-only plan: rewrite the authoring card section 6 Acceptance line so each phase line must name a repo-relative path or symbol and the command that proves the phase done, promoting section 7's one-file/one-verify discipline one level up. One existing line pair, no new file, hook, command or agent.

Measured cost: the three YAMLs total 3159 lines and 218859 bytes versus 81569 bytes for the chat-path docs (AGENTS.md 27372, SKILL.md 28185, ROUTER.md 26012), so loading workflows wholesale is unaffordable while a 1-2 KB step reference costs roughly 250-500 tokens but is a new file.

ROUTER.md carries no plan-quality or review signal; its only quality pointer is an ON_DEMAND row reading Deep-dive quality standards, and SKILL.md references review only as /speckit:complete Step 11 behaviour, which makes the authoring card the cheapest carrier for any new check.
A check can only protect a chat session if it runs before the writes it is meant to govern; a completion-time gate cannot prevent the work, only reject it.
Any mechanism duplicating a check validate.sh already enforces adds no protection and only adds per-turn token cost.
